BiblicalUsage: Once, in the song: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib. The name is read as a man's name, Amminadib, and as a phrase, my noble people, the chariots of my willing people — and the scholars have argued ever since which it is; the verse is the only place the name occurs, and the argument is older than the translations.
TheologicalSignificance: A name that may be a phrase carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is the honesty of the text, that the song leaves the chariots unexplained and the reader must hold both readings at once.
